DayOff Mate (연차메이트) Without sign-in, records stay on your phone

DayOff Mate Privacy Policy

Effective November 23, 2026 · App: DayOff Mate (연차메이트) · Package com.blessingq.dayoffmate · Developer: JAEYOUNG LEE (blessingq)

This English version is a translation provided for convenience. If it differs from the Korean version, the Korean version prevails.

At a glance

  • If you use the app without signing in, your hire date, leave records and notes are stored only on your phone and never sent to the developer's servers.
  • For now, your records stay only on your phone even if you sign in. The server stores only what is needed to verify your account. Once record sync and groups launch, your records will be stored in Google Firebase (Seoul region).
  • Groups (coming later) will only see what you choose to share. Notes, hire date and day adjustments are never shared.
  • Calendar events are read and written only on your phone. Google Drive auto-backup is saved in your own Google Drive; the developer cannot receive or see it.
  • We send usage statistics to improve features. They do not use the advertising ID, are not linked to your account, and can be turned off in Settings.
  • The Android app shows one banner ad on the Home tab. For this, Google processes the advertising ID and related information (section 9).

JAEYOUNG LEE (blessingq, the “developer”) processes the personal information of people who use the mobile app DayOff Mate (연차메이트, package com.blessingq.dayoffmate, the “app”) in accordance with the Korean Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA) and related laws, and publishes this policy under Article 30 of PIPA. It applies to the Android app and the future iOS app.

The current version does not yet offer record sync, groups or notifications. Items 2 to 4 of section 1 and the related parts (leave settings, records and notifications in section 2.2, section 2.3, the group and sync parts of sections 5 and 6, and the camera and notification permissions in section 10) apply from the day each feature launches, and we will announce it in the app when it does. They are marked “(coming later)” in this policy. In the current version, signing in stores on the server only the sign-in provider identifier, app user ID, email address (Google sign-in), sign-in method, sign-up time, the times you confirmed being 14+ and gave consent, and the server access and error logs in section 2.4 (for Google sign-in, also the basic profile kept by the authentication service; see section 2.2).

1. Purposes of processing

  1. Sign-up and account management: verifying sign-in (Kakao, Naver, Google; Apple on iOS), confirming you are 14 or older, recording consent to the Terms and the Privacy Policy, deleting accounts, answering inquiries and verifying identity
  2. Sync (coming later): storing your leave settings, records, day adjustments and settings in your account so you can use them on another phone
  3. Groups (coming later): creating, inviting and joining groups, showing your days off to group members at the level you choose, finding common days off, and (if you allow it) letting people find you by your ID
  4. Notifications (coming later): sending push notifications about group members' days off and join requests. Your own leave and expiry reminders are scheduled on your phone and do not go through the server.
  5. Reliability and security: finding the cause of server errors, checking requests come from the genuine app, preventing abuse (rate limits)
  6. Improvement: per-feature usage statistics (when “Send usage statistics” is on)
  7. Advertising: a banner ad on the Home tab that keeps the app free (Android app)
  8. User protection: handling reports and violations of the Terms

2. Information we process and how we collect it

We process the following personal information without consent under Article 15(1)(4) of PIPA (entering into and performing a contract): sign-in provider identifier, app user ID, email address (Google sign-in), sign-in method, sign-up time, the times you confirmed being 14+ and gave consent, server access and error logs, and app check information. You can turn off usage statistics in the app settings, and delete or reset the advertising ID used for ads as described in section 9.

2.1 Without signing in

There is no account and nothing personal is stored on the developer's servers. Your hire date, leave basis, workplace size, workplace type, weekend setting, leave records (type, date, AM/PM, hours, note), day adjustments and app settings are stored only on your phone. Section 2.4 (automatically generated information) applies whether or not you sign in.

The app does not save the provider's name or profile photo as app data. However, for Google and Apple sign-in, the authentication service (Firebase Authentication) may keep the basic profile passed by the provider (name, profile photo URL) in its sign-in record; the app does not use it on screen or in groups.

  • Nickname (required), ID (optional), whether others may find you by ID

  • Reports, if you file one

2.5 When you contact us, send feedback or ask for deletion

Your email address, the content of your message, and the details you give to verify your identity: sign-in method, sign-in email, nickname, ID, group names and roughly when you signed up. If you use “Send feedback to the developer”, the email body automatically includes the app version, OS version, device manufacturer and model, and app language; you can delete them before sending.

How we collect it

You enter it in the app; we receive it from the sign-in provider; it is generated while you use the app; or you send it by email. The first time you sign in with Kakao, Kakao shows an “app connection” screen; if you connect, Kakao provides your member number to DayOff Mate. Disconnecting the app on the Kakao, Naver or Google side does not delete your DayOff Mate account, so please delete your account in the app or as described on the account deletion page.

3. Information processed only on your phone

The following stays on your phone (or in your own Google account). The developer cannot receive or see it.

  • Records of users who do not sign in: everything in section 2.1. In the current version, records of signed-in users also stay only on the phone.
  • Calendar events: if you turn on “Add days off to calendar” or “Show calendar events”, the app reads and writes your phone's calendar on the phone only. Events are never sent to or stored on our servers, and never included in groups, usage statistics or backups. Events the app adds are titled just “Day off” (no leave type); notes are added only if you turn on “Include notes” (never for health leave). By default events go into a “DayOff Mate” calendar that exists only on this phone. If you choose a calendar from another account such as Google, those events sync with that service under its policy.
  • Google Drive auto-backup (if you turn it on): your records are saved in a hidden, app-only space (the app data folder) in your own Google Drive, sent directly from your phone to your Drive without passing through our servers. The developer cannot receive or see them. One file per day is kept for the last 14 days; a file contains your hire date, leave settings, leave records (including notes) and day adjustments. The Google account email used for backup is stored only on your phone, and may be included in operating-system backups if “Phone backups” below is on. See section 4.
  • Exported backup files: saved or sent to the place you choose (phone storage, your cloud, a messenger). Files contain your hire date, records and notes, so do not send them to others.
  • Home widgets: your remaining leave and upcoming days off (dates and leave types, including health leave) are built on the phone and shown on the home screen, and are not sent to the server. Others can see your home screen, so remove the widget if you don't want this.
  • Your own leave and expiry reminders (coming later): scheduled on the phone.
  • Invite QR scanning (coming later): the camera image is used on the phone only to read the QR code and is not saved or sent.
  • Leave-pay estimate: the pay you enter (monthly, annual or hourly) to estimate pay for unused leave is used on the phone only for the calculation and is never saved. It is not sent to our servers, groups or usage statistics, is not included in any backup (Google Drive auto-backup, backup files or phone backups), and is erased when you close the screen. While this screen is open, Android blocks screenshots and the recent-apps preview.
  • Phone backups: if Android auto-backup or device-to-device transfer is on, the operating system may copy the app's records to your Google account backup or a new phone. This is an operating-system feature; the developer has no access.

4. Google user data (Google API Services User Data Policy)

  • Scope requested: when you turn on Google Drive auto-backup, the app requests only https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.appdata. This scope only gives access to the hidden app folder DayOff Mate creates; the app cannot see or change any other files in your Drive. Google sign-in receives only basic profile information such as your account identifier and email.
  • Use: only to save backup files, list backups with their record counts, restore a backup you choose, and delete backups older than 14 days. Google sign-in information is used only to identify and manage your account.
  • Transfer and sharing: Drive data moves only between your phone and your Google Drive. It is not sent to the developer's servers or to any third party, not used for advertising, marketing, credit assessment or sale, and not read by humans. It is not used to develop, improve or train generalized AI or machine-learning models.
  • Limited Use: DayOff Mate's use and transfer to any other app of information received from Google APIs will adhere to the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.
  • Turning off and deleting: turn off auto-backup in the app under Settings > Backup (files already saved stay in your Drive). Delete saved files in Google Drive on the web: Settings > Manage apps > DayOff Mate > Options > “Delete hidden app data”. Revoke access in your Google Account under Third-party apps & services.

5. Retention and deletion

We delete personal information without delay once its purpose is fulfilled or its retention period ends. When you delete your account, your account data on the server is deleted without delay; the items below are deleted automatically after the periods shown.

Retention periods
InformationRetention
Account (after launch: leave settings, records, group data)Until you delete your account
Individually deleted records and adjustments (coming later)Kept as a “deleted” marker so other phones learn of the deletion; permanently removed within 30 days
Accounts that signed in but did not finish sign-upDeleted immediately if you choose “Not now” or “I'm under 14” on the sign-up screen. If you close the app on the sign-up screen, the sign-up screen is shown again the next time you open it. An account that could not be deleted (for example, because of a network problem) is deleted when you ask us by email (automatic deletion after 24 hours is planned)
Invite codes and links / ID invitations / pending join requests (coming later)Deleted after 48 hours / 14 days / 7 days
Group activity log, records of removed members (coming later)Deleted after 30 days
Device push tokens (coming later)Deleted on sign-out or account deletion, or when the token becomes invalid
Retry data for unlinking Kakao (Kakao member number)Only if unlinking Kakao failed during account deletion; deleted once unlinking succeeds (up to 30 days)
Server access and error logs (Google Cloud Logging)30 days
One-time sign-in valuesExpire within 5 minutes and are deleted automatically within 24 hours after expiry
Rate-limit counters (a hash of the installation ID)Expire 24 hours after the last sign-in attempt and are deleted automatically within 24 hours after expiry
Server backups for disaster recovery (planned)Up to 7 days
Firebase Authentication recordsRemoved from Google's backup systems within 180 days after account deletion (access IP logs: a few weeks)
Usage statistics (Google Analytics)The retention period set in Google Analytics (up to 14 months)
Firebase installation IDPer Google Firebase policy; removed from Google's systems within 180 days after a deletion request
Inquiry and deletion-request emails1 year after the request is handled

No information currently has to be kept under other laws. If paid features are introduced and records such as payment history must be kept, we will update this policy.

How we delete: data is deleted by server functions (automatic expiry policies and the account-deletion function) when its period ends or when you ask; electronic files are deleted so they cannot be recovered. We keep no paper records. Information that exists only on your phone can be deleted with “Delete all records” in the app or by uninstalling the app.

6. Sharing with third parties and group visibility

The developer does not provide or sell your personal information to third parties, except where required by law or requested by investigative authorities through legal procedures.

Groups (coming later) show information to members of the same group based on the consent you give when you first create or join a group (“I agree to show the information above to members of this group”).

Group visibility
RecipientsInformation shownPurposePeriod
Members of groups you join (up to 30 per group) Nickname, group role, dates off with full day/AM/PM/partial. With “with leave types”, leave type and hours. With “show remaining leave”, remaining leave and its as-of date. Only records from 12 months ago to 24 months ahead. Seeing days off together, finding common days off, group leave notifications Until you leave or are removed, or the group or your account is deleted
  • Notes, hire date and tenure, leave basis, day adjustments, expiry dates, workplace size and type, email and sign-in method are never shared. Health leave always appears only as “Day off”. Turning on “Hide from groups” on a record removes it from all groups.
  • Group owners cannot see beyond the level each member chose.
  • If a member turns on group leave notifications, the information you share may also appear in their phone notifications (including the lock screen).
  • After you leave a group or it is deleted, information may remain briefly in other members' app caches.
  • If you turn on “Let others find me by ID”, people who know your exact ID can find and invite you.
  • When you invite via KakaoTalk or the share sheet, your nickname, the group name and the invite code or link are sent by you through the app you choose.

9. Advertising and behavioral information

The Android app shows one Google AdMob banner ad below the record list on the Home tab. Other screens and widgets have no ads, and the iOS app has no ads yet. To show the ad, the Google Mobile Ads SDK built into the app sends the following information to Google LLC.

Behavioral information used for ads
Company that processes itGoogle LLC (Google AdMob)
ItemsAdvertising ID (Android advertising ID) and app set ID, ad impressions and clicks, app use such as app launches and their times, device and OS information, IP address (may be used to estimate approximate location), ad SDK diagnostics
HowSent automatically by the Google Mobile Ads SDK while you use the app
PurposesServing ads, frequency capping, measuring ad performance, preventing click fraud, and (where permitted) personalized ads
RetentionPer Google's policies
How to refuseDelete or reset your advertising ID in your phone settings under Privacy (or Google) > Ads. In regions where consent is required, such as Europe, a Google consent form appears when you first open the app, and you can choose again under Settings > About > Ad privacy settings in the app. In other regions (including Korea) the app has no menu to turn off personalized ads.

The developer does not use this information to identify you and does not use sensitive behavioral information such as health for ads (ad requests contain no records such as leave types or notes). See how Google uses information for ads.

All app permissions are optional; if you decline, everything else keeps working. When you turn on a feature, the app explains it first and then opens the system permission dialog.

11. Your rights and how to exercise them

You may at any time ask to access, correct, delete or stop processing your personal information, and withdraw consent.

  • In the app: edit leave settings (Settings > My leave info), delete records (Settings > Data > Delete all records), delete your account (Settings > Account > “Signed in with …” > Delete account), turn off usage statistics (Settings > About > Send usage statistics). Once groups launch, you can also change your nickname or ID, change your sharing level or leave a group in the app (coming later).
  • By email: write to ejok9194@gmail.com. After verifying your identity we will act without delay (within 10 days) and tell you the result. Account deletion requests are handled within 7 days as described on the account deletion page.
  • You may also act through a legal representative or an authorized person; we may ask for a power of attorney.
  • If the law requires us to refuse or limit a request, we will tell you why.
  • The app's leave calculation is done on your phone for your reference; the developer makes no automated decisions about you.

12. Children under 14

People under 14 cannot sign up (sign in). If you choose “I'm under 14” on the sign-up screen, the sign-in information received is deleted immediately (if it cannot be deleted because of a network problem, it is handled like “accounts that did not finish sign-up” in section 5). You can still use the record features without signing in; in that case no personal information is collected other than the automatically generated information in section 2.4. If we learn that we have collected personal information from a child under 14, we delete it without delay.

13. Security measures

  • Administrative: minimizing the information processed (e.g. only the member number from Kakao); access to admin consoles limited to the developer
  • Technical: encryption in transit (HTTPS/TLS) and at rest (Google Cloud default encryption); security rules that block the app from reading or writing the server database directly (after launch: only you can read your data and only members can read group data, and server rules reject notes or health-leave types in shared data); App Check so only the genuine app can make requests; rate limits on sign-in (after launch, also on invite codes and ID search); support for hiding notification content on the lock screen (coming later)
  • Physical: servers and data are protected by the physical security of Google's data centers (processor)

14. Cookies and similar technologies

The app does not use cookies; it uses the device identifiers in section 2.4 (Firebase installation ID, app instance ID, advertising ID). You can turn off usage statistics in the app and reset the advertising ID in your phone settings. This website (blessingq.github.io/dayoffmate) uses no cookies or visitor tracking.
